A1.justification: Both complete 13-page PDFs describe the same Horizon-Length Prediction work. Text and visual inspection cover Sections 1–7, Figures 1–4, Tables 1–15, and Appendix A.1–A.6, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original controlled model-training experiments on code infilling, repair and reasoning, together with probing and ablation results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including model comparisons in Tables 3–5 and probing, sensitivity and ablation outcomes in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: The auxiliary horizon-prediction head, normalized targets, combined NTP/HLP objective and inference procedure are unchanged. The separate line-horizon prediction adaptation for left-to-right training already appears in v3 Appendix A.5.

E1.justification: Both retain the same training languages and evaluation coverage: SAFIM, CrossCodeEval/CrossCodeLongEval, RepoEval, Defects4J, CRUXEval, and the appendix HumanEval/MBPP evaluations, including their plus variants.

E2.justification: The same DeepSeek-Coder-Base 1.3B/6.7B and StarCoder2 3B/7B NTP baselines participate in corresponding comparisons. Appendix A.3 retains the same four-token prediction comparator.

E3.justification: Training budgets, data processing, evaluation metrics, decoding and sampling settings, and probing splits are unchanged. Both retain 200K-step main training and the 100K-step lambda study in Appendix A.1.

E4.justification: The horizon probes, suffix-attention analysis, planning-failure analysis and appendix studies are retained. No changes occur to the lambda, head-complexity, token-supervision or target-normalization ablations.

E5.justification: Both report the same paired t-tests at p<0.05, significance markers and appendix head-complexity significance discussion. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 2–15 and plotted findings in Figures 3–4 match. For example, Table 3 retains DS-1.3B SAFIM averages of 47.7 without HLP and 50.0 with HLP; Table 15 retains 50.0 for normalized targets versus 34.9 for raw targets.

T1.justification: The FIM sequence definition, normalized horizon target and loss equations (1)–(5) retain the same mathematics, as do the appendix formulations. Equation (1) is rewrapped and partly resized without changing its content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about planning-aware infilling, up to 24% relative improvement, code-reasoning benefits, negligible training overhead and zero additional inference cost.

C2.justification: Interpretations of probing, suffix attention, planning failures and left-to-right performance effects remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning models no larger than 7B parameters and the focus on code.

D1.justification: Optimizer settings, learning-rate rule, batch size, file packing and appendix implementation details are retained. No code or data access disclosure changes; the updated author contact information is administrative.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to conventional FIM, lookahead decoding and multi-token prediction.

P1.justification: v4 updates affiliations, email addresses and the work-location footnote, and makes a few wording corrections, including restoring the missing word in 'models’ hidden states' in Section 5.1. Section order and the main-text/appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 reformats the author block, removes printed page numbers and adjusts Equation (1)'s wrapping and sizing. Figures and tables retain their content, structure and placement, with only small spacing and caption adjustments.

improvement.justification: Repairing the probing sentence in Section 5.1 and reflowing Equation (1) provide small readability benefits, while printed page numbers disappear. The scientific argument, complete empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged; these limited editorial adjustments do not materially alter overall paper quality.
